audit_findings.title: Current diluted shares are paired with a pre-leverage interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: Gross debt increased $371.1 million from $5,114.2 million to $5,485.3 million; first-half interest expense increased $9.5 million; the 120.613896 million denominator is 3.486104 million, or 2.81%, below 2025 diluted weighted-average shares
audit_findings.mechanism: The current share denominator raises per-share value while the historical OE anchor omits the additional after-tax interest associated with the newer borrowing.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense decreased in 2025 when compared to 2024 primarily due to lower weighted average debt balances during 2025 compared to 2024, partially offset by a higher weighted average cost of debt in 2025 when compared to 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated. However, even annualizing the filed $9.5 million first-half interest increase and applying the filed 27.3% interim tax rate produces about $13.8 million of additional annual after-tax interest, only 3.7% of the $377.1 million anchor. Correcting it would reduce value by roughly a few percent and cannot reverse a valuation range already 71.5%-80.4% below the $177.05 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2026 debt proceeds and repurchases, calculate the sustainable after-tax interest on net post-year-end borrowing, and rerun the anchor with that charge while retaining the current fully diluted denominator.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require acquisition spending omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed acquisition amounts include approximately $870 million of 2023 BVS consideration, $74.1 million of 2025 acquisition cash outflow, and the announced $750 million Círculo de Crédito enterprise value; $750 million equals 13.7% of the $5,469 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings can increase historical OE and support forecast growth, while purchase prices are excluded from ordinary capital expenditures and therefore from the modeled reinvestment requirement.
audit_findings.evidence: A critical lever of our strategy is inorganic growth through accretive and strategic acquisitions that drive incremental annual revenue growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that acquisitions are a critical growth lever and that individual transactions are large relative to the valuation. It does not establish what portion of the 3%-5% growth assumptions is organic or the normalized acquisition spending required. Because omitted recurring acquisition reinvestment could materially reduce the base and bull values, this remains open and material.
audit_findings.action: Build an organic-versus-acquired revenue and OE bridge for each historical acquisition, estimate a normalized acquisition-spend requirement supported by filed transaction data, and rerun the growth scenarios after deducting that requirement or using demonstrably organic growth rates.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retirement claims are absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: The filed 2025 pension funded-status deficit was $106.4 million, including $82.6 million for unfunded supplemental plans; $106.4 million equals 1.95% of base equity value and $0.88 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A debt-like pension deficit would reduce the equity bridge unless its future settlement cash flows are already fully captured in forecast OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The projected benefit obligation and accumulated benefit obligation for these plans in the aggregate were $ 82.6 million and $ 84.4 million at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, and these plans did not have any plan assets at December 31, 2025 or 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but its filed scale is limited. A full dollar-for-dollar deduction of the entire $106.4 million deficit would reduce base value from $45.34 to approximately $44.46 per share and would not alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Update the funded status and expected contributions through June 2026, then either deduct the remaining debt-like deficit or document where all settlement cash flows are included in forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interest needs an explicit bridge reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: The filed redeemable noncontrolling interest was $121.5 million at June 30, 2026, equal to 2.22% of base equity value and $1.01 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A future put payment reduces parent cash, while purchasing the minority interest adds the related minority cash flows to Equifax owners; both sides must be modeled together.
audit_findings.evidence: These shares were issued with specific rights allowing the holders to sell the shares back to Equifax, at fair value during specified future time periods starting at the fifth anniversary and only when certain conditions exist.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing reconciliation is demonstrated, but a valuation overstatement is not: attributable earnings already exclude the minority interest, and redemption transfers the associated earnings interest to Equifax. Even treating the entire current balance as a deduction with no added cash flows would reduce base value by only about $1.01 per share and would not change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the current redemption value, exercise conditions and earliest exercise date, and calculate the present value of the put together with the incremental minority OE acquired.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified legal and regulatory exposure may exceed recorded costs
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional settlements, penalties, remediation and recurring compliance costs would reduce OE; operational restrictions could also reduce forecast growth.
audit_findings.evidence: For certain of these matters, it is reasonably possible that we will incur losses, however it is not possible at this time to estimate the amount of loss or range of possible losses that might result from their resolution.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing expressly establishes reasonably possible additional losses but provides no estimable amount or range. Recorded amounts include a $30 million 2025 inquiry-dispute accrual and a separate $100 million 2026 FCRA settlement accrual offset by a $60 million insurance receivable, but those amounts do not quantify the CFPB, antitrust and other unresolved exposures. The possibility is real, while the record cannot establish whether the incremental effect is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain post-filing case developments, claimed damages, insurance limits, legal probability assessments and any new accruals for the CFPB investigation, Workforce Solutions antitrust litigation and other proceedings; rerun OE and growth only when incremental cash costs or operating restrictions become estimable.
